content.heading: ✅ Q1: Choose the Correct Statement for Each of the Following

content.problemHtml:
When a coil rotates inside a uniform magnetic field at a constant angular speed, the induced voltage obtained is:

  • a- Constant in magnitude
  • b- Constant in direction
  • c- Sinusoidal alternating
  • d- Pulsed

steps.note: Rotating the coil at a constant angular speed inside a uniform field produces a voltage that varies as a sinusoidal function of time (as in the stages of Figure 3-11).

content.problemHtml:
The basis of how metal detectors work is:

  • a- Lenz's law
  • b- Eddy currents
  • c- Faraday's phenomenon
  • d- The phenomenon of self-induction

steps.note: Metal detectors work based on eddy currents induced in nearby metal pieces.

content.problemHtml:
A DC generator contains:

  • a- An induction coil
  • b- Two slip rings
  • c- The commutator
  • d- None of the above

steps.note: A DC generator replaces the two slip rings with a commutator made of two insulated halves to maintain a constant direction of current.

content.problemHtml:
A motor converts electrical energy into:

  • a- Mechanical energy
  • b- Thermal energy
  • c- Light energy
  • d- Chemical energy

steps.note: A motor is a device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy in the presence of a magnetic field.

content.problemHtml:
The self-inductance of a coil depends on:

  • a- The shape of the coil
  • b- The length of the coil and the area of a single turn
  • c- The number of turns of the coil
  • d- All of the above

steps.note: The self-inductance depends on the coil's geometric shape, core material, length, area of a single turn, and number of turns, all together.

solution.final: ✓ Correct answer: d — All of the above
solution.label: Solution

content.problemHtml: State the parts of an AC generator, with a diagram.
content.label: Q2

steps.note: Four main parts: (1) The armature — an insulated coil that rotates about an axis in a uniform magnetic field. (2) The magnet — permanent or electric, surrounding the armature. (3) The two slip rings — rotate with the coil, each connected to one of its ends. (4) The two brushes — made of carbon, connecting the slip rings to the external circuit.

solution.final: ✓ Four parts: the armature, the magnet, the two slip rings, the two brushes
solution.label: Answer

content.label: Q3

steps.note: We apply the right-hand rule (index finger = field B, thumb = motion of the conductor v, middle finger = current I) to each of the four cases.

content.problemHtml: Does Lenz's law satisfy the principle of conservation of energy? Explain.
content.label: Q4

steps.note: Yes, Lenz's law satisfies the principle of conservation of energy. The induced magnetic field resulting from the induced current generates a force opposing the motion of the conductor, and external work must be done to overcome this opposing force; it is this work that is converted into the energy of the induced current (heat, mechanical work, or chemical energy).

If the opposite were true (i.e., the induced current reinforced the change that caused it instead of opposing it), energy would amplify itself without any external energy source, which violates the principle of conservation of energy.

solution.final: ✓ Yes; the resulting opposing force requires external work that converts into the energy of the induced current, consistent with conservation of energy
solution.label: Answer

content.problemHtml: Explain the method for determining the direction of the current in the armature of an electric generator.
content.label: Q5

steps.note: The right-hand rule is used: the fingers of the right hand (thumb, index, and middle) are placed perpendicular to each other; the index finger points in the direction of the magnetic field, the thumb points in the direction of motion of the conductor (the armature), while the middle finger points in the direction of the induced current in it.

solution.final: ✓ Using the right-hand rule (index = field, thumb = motion, middle = current)
solution.label: Answer

content.problemHtml: How can an AC generator be modified to generate a direct current?
content.label: Q6

steps.note: By replacing the two separate slip rings with a single ring split into two electrically insulated halves (the commutator), while ensuring that the connection of one brush switches from one half to the other exactly at the moment the induced voltage tries to reverse its direction, which keeps the current direction in the external circuit constant (though in the form of pulses of varying magnitude).

solution.final: ✓ Replacing the two slip rings with a commutator of two insulated halves synchronized with the voltage reversal
solution.label: Answer

content.problemHtml: A coil with 6 turns and an area of \((10\ \text{cm}^2)\) is placed in a magnetic field of flux density \((0.1\ \text{T})\). The field changes over a time interval of \((1\times10^{-3}\ \text{s})\). Find the magnitude of the induced electromotive force generated across the coil, given that the magnetic field acts perpendicular to the coil's surface.
content.label: Problem 1

given: \( \Delta B = 0.1\ \text{T} \) — the change in magnetic flux density (fully disappears or appears)

steps.note: Since the field acts perpendicular to the coil's surface, \(\Delta\varnothing = A\Delta B\)

solution.label: Detailed Solution

content.problemHtml: A coil with 100 turns and an area of \((5\ \text{cm}^2)\) is in a uniform magnetic field of flux density \((0.25\ \text{T})\) acting perpendicular to the surface. The coil was pulled quickly and, within \((0.01\ \text{s})\), left the magnetic field. Find: 1- The induced electromotive force. 2- The electric charge passing through the coil, given that the coil's resistance equals \((20\ \Omega)\).
content.label: Problem 2

given: \( B_i = 0.25\ \text{T},\ B_f = 0 \) — the coil fully leaves the field
solution.required: 1- Calculate \(\varepsilon_{ind}\). 2- Calculate the electric charge q passing through the coil.

steps.note: 1- We apply Faraday's law, where \(\Delta\varnothing=A\Delta B\)
2- We first calculate the current from Ohm's law, then the charge \(q=I\Delta t\)

solution.label: Detailed Solution

content.problemHtml: How many turns are needed to generate an electromotive force of \((10\ \text{V})\) in a coil moving inside a magnetic flux changing at a rate of \((5\times10^{-3}\ \text{weber/s})\)?
content.label: Problem 3

given: \( \dfrac{\Delta\varnothing}{\Delta t} = 5\times10^{-3}\ \text{Wb/s} \) — the rate of change of flux (per turn)
solution.required: Calculate the number of turns N needed.

steps.note: From Faraday's law, rearranging to solve for N

solution.label: Detailed Solution

questions.question: Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction is:
Lenz's law determines:
options: The magnitude of the induced current only
The direction of the induced current (opposes the change that causes it)
questions.explain: Lenz's law determines the direction of the induced current, which opposes the magnetic change that causes it.

questions.question: Eddy currents are a phenomenon that:
options: Can have its thermal damage reduced by using thin insulated laminations
Is always beneficial with no drawbacks
questions.explain: Eddy currents cause thermal loss, and their damage is reduced by using thin insulated laminations instead of a solid metal piece.

questions.question: The difference between an AC generator and a DC generator is:
options: The rotation speed of the armature only
The use of two slip rings versus a commutator
questions.explain: An AC generator uses two separate slip rings, while a DC generator replaces them with a commutator of two insulated halves.

questions.question: The back electromotive force of a motor arises because of:
options: A rise in the motor's temperature
The rotation of the motor's coil inside the magnetic field (per Faraday and Lenz)
A weak battery feeding the motor
questions.explain: The rotation of the motor's coil generates an electromotive force according to Faraday, which opposes the source voltage according to Lenz, and is called the back electromotive force.

summary.heading: 📋 Chapter Three Summary
items: Faraday's law: \(\varepsilon_{ind}=-N\Delta\varnothing/\Delta t\) — a change in magnetic flux generates an induced electromotive force.
Lenz's law: the induced current's direction opposes the change that causes it, satisfying the principle of conservation of energy.
Eddy currents cause thermal loss, and metal objects are made as insulated laminations to reduce them.
Self-induction: \(\varepsilon_{ind}=-L\Delta I/\Delta t\), and the self-inductance \(L=N\Delta\varnothing/\Delta I\).
A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy (alternating with two slip rings, or direct with a commutator), and a motor works in reverse.
A motor's torque arises from a force couple, and a back electromotive force arises in it while it rotates.
